parts.title: Campus Conversation: Buying a Meal Plan
script: Listen to a conversation between a student and a worker at the campus cafeteria.
Hi. Welcome to the cafeteria. What would you like?
Hello. I want to buy a meal plan. How does it work?
You pay money at the start of the month. Then you can eat here every day.
The small plan is one hundred dollars. It has twenty meals. The big plan is one hundred and fifty dollars. It has forty meals.
I eat here only at lunch. I think the small plan is better for me.
Okay. Do you eat meat? Some meals are only for people who eat vegetables.
I eat meat, but I like vegetables too.
Good. Then you can choose any meal. I need your student card to make the plan.
Here it is. Can I pay with a credit card?
Yes, you can. Just put your card in the machine over there.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.exp: The student asks how a meal plan works and buys one.

questions.q: How much is the small plan?
questions.exp: The woman says the small plan is one hundred dollars.

questions.q: Why does the student choose the small plan?
o: He eats here only at lunch
He does not like the food
questions.exp: He says he eats here only at lunch.

questions.q: Listen again: "I need your student card to make the plan." Why does the woman say this?
questions.exp: She needs the card to make the plan.

questions.q: What will the student probably do next?
questions.exp: He asks about paying by card and she says yes.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: Why Do Earthquakes Happen?
script: Listen to part of a lecture in a geography class.
Today we will talk about earthquakes. An earthquake is a strong shaking of the ground.
The surface of the Earth is made of big pieces of rock. We call them plates. The plates move very slowly, only a few centimeters each year.
Sometimes two plates push against each other. They get stuck. For many years, the pressure grows.
Then, suddenly, the rock breaks and the plates move. This sends waves through the ground. The waves make the ground shake. This is an earthquake.
Most earthquakes happen near the edges of plates. For example, Japan and Chile have many earthquakes because they are near the edges of plates.
Scientists cannot say exactly when an earthquake will come. But they use special machines to measure the shaking.
People who live in these places must be ready. Strong buildings help a lot. Also, people should know a safe place to go, such as under a strong table.
Next week, we will talk about how people build safe buildings.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
questions.exp: The professor explains how plates cause earthquakes.

o: Big pieces of rock on the Earth's surface
questions.exp: Plates are big pieces of rock.

questions.q: What happens when the plates get stuck?
questions.exp: For many years, the pressure grows.

questions.q: Listen again: "For example, Japan and Chile have many earthquakes." Why does the professor say this?
o: To say these places are dangerous to visit
To show places near the edges of plates
questions.exp: They are examples of places near plate edges.

questions.q: What can help people in earthquake places?
questions.exp: The professor says strong buildings help a lot.

questions.q: What will the class probably discuss next week?
questions.exp: She says next week they will talk about safe buildings.
